audit.title: CCIP Architecture

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with "This section explains the core architecture..." — a meta-description, not an answer. It never states in a liftable sentence *what CCIP's architecture is*. Weak for a page that owns the word "architecture."

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1 + 4 bolded, linked bullets; 0 level skips, 95-word section. Good for its size, but a single flat list is the whole page — no depth to chunk.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 3 numerals, 0 with units, no versions. Effectively no specifics — expected for an index, but it means zero quantitative lift.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 internal links, 0 external. Appropriate for a hub, but no link to a canonical CCIP concept page or primary source elevates trust.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Expands "Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP)" but gives no crisp one-sentence definition an engine can lift. Missed cheap win.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no og/twitter tags, no schema dates. A visible "Last Updated: 2025-06-09" exists in markdown but isn't in structured metadata. Weak; head metadata could not be verified from the capture (CLI should pass raw `<head>`).

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code — genuinely not applicable for an index page; not penalized as a defect.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the four architecture subtopics (overview, key concepts, onchain, offchain) but only as labels; no "how does CCIP work" / "what are CCIP components" phrasing to win retrieval.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Minor: "EVM smart contracts and Solana programs, and Aptos modules" has an awkward comma.

audit.summary: This is a thin section-index page (98 words, 1 heading, 4 links) whose job is to route readers to the CCIP architecture sub-pages. Its strength is clean, unambiguous prose with a consistent product name; its biggest weakness is that it carries almost no liftable substance — no self-contained definition, no specifics, no metadata — so a generative engine has little reason to retrieve or cite it over the deeper child pages it points to. The honest verdict: acceptable as navigation, but it forfeits nearly all direct-citation value it could cheaply capture by adding a short canonical definition and a one-line summary of each component. As an index, judge it lightly on code — but its metadata gaps are real and fixable.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical, liftable definition of CCIP architecture
recommendations.where: First paragraph, replacing/augmenting "This section explains the core architecture..."
recommendations.issue: "This section explains the core architecture of the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol"
recommendations.change: Lead with a self-contained sentence, e.g. "CCIP's architecture combines onchain components (EVM smart contracts, Solana programs, Aptos modules) with a decentralized offchain network — including the Risk Management Network — to enable secure cross-chain messaging and token transfers."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-quotable answer to "what is CCIP architecture," which the current meta-description cannot supply.

recommendations.title: Annotate each component link with a one-line value statement
recommendations.issue: Bullets describe only *what the page is* ("Get a high-level summary"), not *what the component does*.
recommendations.change: Append a fact to each, e.g. "**Onchain Components** — the Router, OnRamp/OffRamp, and Token Pool contracts that execute transfers on each chain."
recommendations.why: Turns a bare link list into extractable reasons/facts, improving retrieval for component-name queries.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD and a canonical URL
recommendations.issue: Measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, dateModified absent from schema.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-06-09`, `inLanguage: en`, and a self-referential `canonical`; surface the "Last Updated" date in structured metadata, not just body text.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and canonical signals raise agent trust/E-E-A-T; measured metadata is currently near-empty.

recommendations.title: Phrase the intro to match how devs ask
recommendations.issue: No "how does CCIP work" / "what are the components of CCIP" phrasing.
recommendations.change: Add a short line: "How does CCIP work? It splits responsibilities across onchain contracts and an offchain oracle network — the components below."
recommendations.why: Question-phrased text wins retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative outbound reference
recommendations.change: Link the Risk Management Network / CCIP whitepaper or security spec once.
recommendations.why: A primary-source link raises citation credibility for an otherwise all-internal hub.

antiPatterns: None material. The page is short but not padded; no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references. Minor grammar nit in the "EVM... Solana... Aptos" clause.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced — good site-level signal; ensure it lists this page and its children.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are template/site-level concerns; verify they're emitted site-wide, not just here.
As a hub page, its citation value depends on child pages earning retrieval; ensure each child links back to this index (canonical-hub pattern).
